key_insight: At shortage prices harvested phone LPDDR is worth more than the phone; a CXL bridge with defect remap gives OEM-rejected packages a datacenter outlet, zero wafer starts.
killer_doubt: Chinese phone OEMs already buy harvested DRAM natively; if they absorb >80% of good pulls the bridge sees only rejects, and underfilled-PoP removal yield below ~70% breaks cost/GB.
decisive_experiment: Buy ~2,000 EOL phones (~$40k), desolder/reball LPDDR4X, test BER and retention at 85 C on an FPGA fixture; build one 128 GB CXL card on an FPGA bridge; report good-GB yield and $/GB.
prior_art: Chinese OEMs reuse desoldered phone DRAM; Meta (Vistara ASIC) and Google reuse DDR4 via CXL (via search snippet). LPDDR-to-CXL bridge: none found.

key_insight: Mature-node DRAM loses ~10-20% of die (more on ramping nodes like 1c) partly to cell faults that a boot-time fault map plus erasure coding could recover at ~2-5% overhead.
killer_doubt: At 1% random faults DDR5 on-die SEC leaves ~39% of 136-bit words uncorrectable; the rate-0.85 LDPC needed costs 15% capacity plus decode latency, eating most of a 10-25% gain.
decisive_experiment: Buy ~500 downgraded/UTT DDR4-DDR5 components from broker channels, map faults over temperature and time on an FPGA tester, classify static vs random vs gross, and compute recoverable good bits per die.
prior_art: ArchShield (Nair, Kim, Qureshi, ISCA 2013) fault-map tolerance; Micron SpecTek downgraded components; DDR5 on-die ECC and post-package repair; Linux page offlining.

key_insight: Pre-2006 DRAM patents are expired, so a 50-90 nm stacked-capacitor flow is legally open; a published map marginally helps specialty and legacy DRAM entrants.
killer_doubt: Legal risk is not the barrier: a 90 nm 8F2 cell is ~65x the area of a 1b cell, so cost/GB is uncompetitive whatever the royalties.
decisive_experiment: Interview 10 prospective legacy/specialty DRAM entrants and their counsel (~$50k); if fewer than 3 rank freedom-to-operate cost above capital and yield know-how as a top-3 barrier, stop.
prior_art: Routine FTO studies by patent firms; legacy and specialty DRAM already made by Winbond, Nanya, ESMT and CXMT without such an atlas.

key_insight: Thermal drawing really does shrink cm-scale multi-material preforms to sub-micron features without lithography; fused fiber faceplates are a cheap large-area structuring method.
killer_doubt: Random access needs row/column lines at cell pitch, which coarse metallization cannot give; at 500 nm core pitch density is ~0.05 GB/cm2, ~100x below 1b DRAM's ~5.5 GB/cm2.
decisive_experiment: Draw a 100-core preform with semiconductor-glass cores and metal gate sheaths in a university draw tower; measure single-core transistor on/off ratio and storage-node retention at 85 C.
prior_art: Multimaterial fiber devices (Fink, MIT; Abouraddy, CREOL); silicon-core fibers (Ballato, Clemson); fused fiber-optic faceplates. Fiber memory arrays: none found.

key_insight: Tacit yield and integration knowledge from closed U.S. and European DRAM fabs is perishable and cheap to capture now, before the people retire out.
killer_doubt: Know-how from 90-40 nm planar fabs transfers poorly to sub-20 nm or oxide 3D processes; it saves an entrant months, not the $15B+ and 3-5 years that gate supply.
decisive_experiment: Pilot 20 structured interviews (~$60k); have a new-entrant process team score transcripts for actionable yield fixes; continue only if over 25% contain process detail absent from the literature.
prior_art: Computer History Museum oral histories; expert networks and retired-engineer consultancies; SEMI and CHIPS Act workforce programs.

key_insight: Sensing every ~32 cells drops bitline capacitance to ~2-3 fF, so ~0.3 fF still gives ~50 mV: the capacitor shrinks ~15x and the 60-75:1 etch disappears.
killer_doubt: Planar MIM in 4F2 at F=12 nm gives ~0.04 fF, not 0.3; and one bond per 32 cells, even shared over 6 decks, needs ~330 nm pitch, beyond hybrid-bonding practice.
decisive_experiment: Tape out a 28 nm MPW test chip with 32-cell micro-bitlines, 0.1-0.5 fF short-pillar or MIM cells and offset-cancelled sense amps; measure signal-margin distribution over 1e5 cells versus Cs.
prior_art: Samsung/SK hynix 4F2 VCT with periphery-under-cell bonding; Phase B N-40 (64-cell bitlines, 8:1 mux, ~1 um bonds) is the feasible-pitch version.

key_insight: Static inference weights need no refresh, restore or writes; ROM storage removes endurance and refresh from that share of memory and cuts access energy.
killer_doubt: Taalas HC1 already puts weights in mask ROM on 6 nm; 28-40 nm via-ROM is ~10-50x less dense than 1b DRAM, so a 4-bit 70B model needs ~7-16 reticle dies.
decisive_experiment: Lay out a 2-bit via-programmed ROM macro in a 28 nm PDK, extract bit density and pJ/bit, and compare $/GB of weights against DRAM at 4x contract price over a 12-month model life.
prior_art: Taalas HC1: Llama 3.1 8B weights in mask ROM on TSMC 6 nm, 2026 (via search snippet); academic ROM-based compute-in-memory macros.

key_insight: Much fleet DRAM holds pages idle for seconds or longer; age-graded compression plus flash offload recovers capacity with logic only, no wafers.
killer_doubt: Already deployed at scale: Meta TMO reports ~20-32% memory savings, not 1.6-2.5x, and Marvell Structera CXL expanders already offer inline LZ4 compression.
decisive_experiment: Replay a production page-access trace through a simulator of the three-tier ladder; compare effective capacity and p99 latency against zswap plus TMO-style offload; proceed only if gain exceeds 1.3x.
prior_art: Google software-defined far memory (ASPLOS 2019), Meta TMO (ASPLOS 2022), Linux zswap, Marvell Structera, ZeroPoint Technologies compression IP.

key_insight: Capacitance scaling with deposited layer count instead of etch aspect ratio is sound in MLCCs and IPDs, and selective lateral recess is proven 3D NAND processing.
killer_doubt: At a ~0.001 um2 cell, cuts and two contacts leave <~30% plate area: ~0.025 area-gain/nm of stack versus ~0.06/nm for a 20 nm pillar, so 2.5-5x taller.
decisive_experiment: In a university nanofab, deposit a 10-pair TiN/HfZrO/Ru stack, etch 100 nm trenches, test TiN-vs-Ru selective recess, and measure capacitance per footprint and edge leakage against a pillar benchmark.
prior_art: Fujitsu fin-type stacked capacitor (IEDM 1988, multi-fin storage node); TSMC multilayer SHDMIM in BEOL; MLCCs; 3D NAND lateral recess.

key_insight: An open, process-parameterized DRAM periphery generator (sense amps, decoders, pumps) would cut design entry cost for new array technologies, especially oxide and gain-cell entrants.
killer_doubt: Incumbents will not donate live patents and pre-2006 ones are already free; DRAM periphery is analog and process-specific, and 0 open DRAM PDKs exist to generate against.
decisive_experiment: Extend OpenRAM to generate a 1T1C/2T0C array with sense amps and charge pumps on SKY130 or GF180, tape out on a free MPW shuttle, and measure yield and timing against predictions.
prior_art: OpenRAM (UCSC) open SRAM compiler; RISC-V and MPEG-LA pool models; commercial memory compilers (Synopsys, Arm); Open Invention Network defensive pooling.

key_insight: A portable, qualified gain-cell macro plus controller RTL lets idle mature logic fabs make on-die and edge memory without DRAM process know-how.
killer_doubt: Logic gain cells at 22-40 nm are ~0.1-0.2 um2/bit, ~50-100x below 1b DRAM: 30 fabs at ~50k wafers/month add ~0.03-0.1 EB/yr, ~0.1-0.4% of world bits.
decisive_experiment: Tape out a 2T/3T gain-cell macro on a 22-40 nm MPW, measure 85 C retention, bit area and refresh power; run a BEOL IGZO 2T0C module at a university fab for comparison.
prior_art: OpenRAM; gain-cell eDRAM macros (Teman, Giterman, Burg groups); Intel and IBM eDRAM; imec and Kioxia IGZO 2T0C; DARPA 3DSoC with SkyWater.

key_insight: PV inline tools process a wafer for well under $1 at ~8,000 wafers/hour, and thickness-defined vertical channels can set one critical dimension without lithography.
killer_doubt: Laser-scribe and screen-print pitches are ~10-40 um, so each bit takes ~100-1,600 um2, ~1e5x less dense than 1b; NAND already serves slow tiers far cheaper.
decisive_experiment: Laser-scribe a PECVD a-Si or IGZO vertical TFT-capacitor array on glass at the finest PV scribe pitch; measure cell pitch, leakage and retention, then compute GB per M10 wafer.
prior_art: Thin-film/TFT memory work in display fabs; Phase B N-38 panel-level oxide memory at F~100 nm imprint is the stronger version.
